title: Social
description: The vocabulary of a social and marketing island: posts, the channels they go out on and visits come through, the conversations they begin, and what each brought, on the shared set alone. The counts a post or a channel carries are kept for an operator outside the map to write; the words of a post are its author's.

types.title: Post
types.description: One post on one channel, written by a person by hand: an agent sets it out empty (what it is for, where it goes, its tagged link). Its tag is the ?ref= its link carries (linkedin-26w46-1: the channel, the year and week, its number that week), so each visit and trial is counted onto the post that brought it. It goes_out_on its channel, and waits_on whoever writes it.

channel.description: Where it goes out: picks the length it is held to.

tag.description: The source tag its link carries (?ref=<tag>): letters, digits, - and _, up to 40. One post, one tag.

url.description: The post itself, once it is out.

replies.description: Replies it drew, as its author counts them.

impressions.description: Times it was seen, as the channel counts them, typed in at about 3 and 7 days. A weak signal: never summed into a judgement.

reactions.description: Likes and other reactions, as the channel counts them. A weak signal.

reposts.description: Reposts and shares, as the channel counts them. A weak signal.

conversations.description: Conversations it began: those that came_out_of it.

visits.description: Page loads under its tag, as the seller counts them: nothing about the visitor is kept.

first_visit.description: The first day a visit was counted under its tag.

last_visit.description: The last day a visit was counted under its tag.

asked.description: Trials asked for under its tag.

paid.description: Trials paid for, and workspaces bought with no trial, under its tag.

ended.description: Trials under its tag that ended unpaid.

types.title: Channel
types.description: Where posts go out (linkedin, x) or visits come through with no post's tag (an agent such as chatgpt, a search engine, a site that linked here). Titled with its name; what came under no post's tag is counted onto it, so each channel is measured beside its posts.

tag.description: The tag its visits carry when no post's does (?ref= or ?utm_source=), as the seller reads it.

visits.description: Page loads under its tag, as the seller counts them: nothing about the visitor is kept.

first_visit.description: The first day a visit was counted under its tag.

last_visit.description: The last day a visit was counted under its tag.

asked.description: Trials asked for under its tag.

paid.description: Trials paid for, and workspaces bought with no trial, under its tag.

ended.description: Trials under its tag that ended unpaid.

types.title: Conversation
types.description: Someone who replied or wrote and said the problem they have. It came_out_of the post that began it, or the channel it came through. Its title is the person and the problem in a few words; its note holds what was said.

person.description: Who it is with: their name or handle.

channel.description: Where it is had; the post's channel unless said.

problem.description: The problem they said, in their words.

types.title: Channel month
types.description: A month of the channels written down once it is over: each channel's posts, visits, trials begun and paid, conversations and hours, and which met the strategy's bar. A finding, so another island may read it across; written by the operator that counts, about each post it counted.

posts.description: Posts that went out that month.

visits.description: Visits under those posts' tags and the channels'.

paid.description: Trials paid for, and workspaces bought, under their tags.

conversations.description: Conversations that month that came out of a post or a channel.

met.description: The channels that met the bar.

links.title: goes out on
links.description: The post goes out on this channel: what the channels view reads its posts from.

links.title: came out of
links.description: The conversation came out of this post, or the channel it came through with no post: what a post's count of conversations is read from.

styles.title: A post's words are its author's
styles.body: Every post, thread, caption and message is written by its author, by hand. Never draft, rewrite or suggest its words. What an agent does: set out each post as an empty document (type social_post, status to_write) with what it is for, where it goes (its channel field and a goes_out_on link to the channel), its tag, and waits_on its author; organise ideas and topics; record what a post brought. How tags and conversations are kept: query with name instructions, params for guide:social.

styles.title: Tag every post's link
styles.body: A post's link carries ?ref=<tag>: its channel, the year and week, its number that week (linkedin-26w46-1). Set the tag when you set out the post; one post, one tag, never reused. Visits and trials are counted onto the post or channel whose tag they carry, by an operator outside the map: never write those counts yourself.

styles.title: Record a conversation
styles.body: When a reply or message says the problem someone has, record it with change: a talk titled with the person and the problem in a few words, its person, problem and began, linked came_out_of the post that began it (or the channel, when no post did). What was said goes in its note, in their words.
